predictions: P-A (BB union rule - a NULL prediction): NO block, resolved or integrated, will pass the union rule (LRT_BANDBB_BAND >= 9.2 AND kT > 1.05) OR (LRT_CPLBB_CPL >= 9.2 AND kT > 1.05). If the new sweep again crowns CPL+BB in blk0 that is NOT a blackbody detection, and must not be reported as one; the BIC winner is CPL in every archival row including blk0.

P-A2 (where the BB would appear IF it appears): the strongest thermal candidate stays in the FIRST block. Archival LRT_CPLBB_CPL by block: blk0 (3.82-10.17 s) = 4.32, blk1 (10.17-22.25 s) = 0.17, blk2 (22.25-28.88 s) = 0.24, integrated = 0.92; and blk0 also carries the LOWEST temperature, kT = 3.77 +/- 1.02 keV (Band+BB) / 3.77 +/- 1.02 keV (CPL+BB) - i.e. the L28 edge-constrained low-kT class, sitting at roughly half the ~8.1 keV NaI low-energy edge. (The other archival kT values - 9.06 +/- 3.86 keV in blk1, 6.73 +/- 2.51 keV in blk2 - all have LRT < 0.4, i.e. they are the unconstrained free parameter of a component the data do not want.)

P-B (integrated shape over the FULL stamped window): the new time-integrated fit over -4.0 -> +78.0 s will select a CURVED, EXPONENTIALLY-CUT model (CPL or its Band/SBPL equivalent with a railed high-energy index) with Ep in 130-175 keV and low-energy index in -1.15 .. -0.75. FALSIFIED IF the integrated Ep falls outside 110-220 keV, or if the AIC winner is a pure power law, or if a well-constrained beta > -3.5 appears (see P-B3). FRAMES TO DIFF AGAINST, each with its component coverage (T9): (i) GBM catalog flnc_comp over -3.072 -> +68.608 s with dets n0,n1,n9,b1 (TTE, Castor C-STAT): Ep = 146.86 +/- 7.92 keV, index = -0.9750 +/- 0.0516, redchisq 1.1162/474 - COVERAGE = TOTAL single pulse; (ii) GBM catalog flnc_band, same window/dets: Ep = 149.67 +/- 11.13, alpha = -0.98645 +/- 0.04286, beta = -8.154 +/- 1586.3 UNCONSTRAINED, redchisq 1.1184/473; (iii) archival prior over 3.82 -> 28.88 s with our own 5 detectors: Band Ep = 153.79 +/- 7.58 keV, alpha = -0.6029 +/- 0.0684, beta = -5.000 RAILED; CPL index = -0.6032, Ec = 110.24 keV -> Ep = (2+alpha)*Ec = 154.0 keV - COVERAGE = 35% of T90, the BRIGHT MIDDLE ONLY. *** COVERAGE PREDICTION, the sharpest falsifiable item here: our new window ADDS the soft rise (-4 -> 3.8 s) and the entire soft decay (28.9 -> 67 s) that the archival window omitted. Our integrated low-energy index must therefore come out SOFTER than the archival -0.603 and land near the catalog's -0.975 +/- 0.052. If the new integrated alpha comes back at -0.60 again, the cause is NOT physics: either the binning again failed to reach past ~29 s, or the background model is wrong. ***

P-B2 (evolution class - hard-to-soft, but WEAK): block-resolved Ep will be monotonically non-increasing with time and the low-energy index monotonically softening, with a SMALL total swing. Archival: Ep(Band) 158.2 -> 154.4 -> 141.1 keV (a mere -11% over 25 s) while alpha runs -0.373 -> -0.593 -> -0.838 (a much larger swing than Ep). PREDICT the same ordering and predict that ALPHA, not Ep, carries the spectral evolution: |dEp/Ep| < 40% across the blocks that overlap 3.8-29 s, while alpha changes by > 0.3. FALSIFIED IF Ep peaks in a middle block by more than its error (intensity tracking), or if alpha HARDENS with time. CAVEAT PUBLISHED IN ADVANCE: with only 3 archival blocks the 'monotonic' claim rests on 3 points and 2 of the 3 Ep values agree within errors (158.2 +/- 14.7 vs 154.4 +/- 9.2) - the honest prior is 'no significant Ep evolution detected', and the monotonic ordering is a weak, easily-falsified pattern, flagged as weak here rather than after the fact.

PREDICT: >= 3 of 4 new rows return beta railed/unconstrained, and the AIC comparison of Band vs CPL favours CPL (fewer parameters, same fit) in the integrated spectrum. FALSIFIED IF the integrated beta is well constrained (error < 0.5) and shallower than -3.5. EXPECT a BOUND_CAPPED diagnosis on beta - this burst should exercise that flag.
